name: 1730 Prairie Avenue — brick house under a mansard with its two-storey rear range, K01 frontage assembly

grade.why: Pictured: a picture on the Images tab shows it.

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1840 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

placement.position_note: The rear south corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 33.400, v 1.000 m from the middle of the rear lot line), read off the 1911 sheet's trace (T-2934) through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check, so its own fit residual, 3.08 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed. Rotation -0.582 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.
placement.symbolic_location: 1730 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1730 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).

footprint.note: The front block read off the 1911 sheet's trace (s20fp-1730-b1 p1) in the draft's lot frame: the sheet draws a wall across the house at u 33.4 between the '3B' front block and the '2B' rear range, the front at 45.9 (12.5 m deep), the south wall at v 1.0 and the north at 8.9, on the lot's north line (7.9 m along the street). The draft took the whole 22.75 m as one three-storey block; the sheet's own line divides it, and the rear range is rear_wings. The block's south projection is K08's (bays).

stories.note: '3B' printed on the front block of the 1911 sheet, and '12 12' against its walls: two storeys of 12-inch brick wall, so the third is not a masonry storey but the roof's. The sheet also draws a dashed line inside the block's walls with a diagonal at each corner, the plan of a roof's deck and hips: a mansard, its storey the '3' (T-2934). 1736 next door, the sheet's other '3B' with a dashed inner line, is a mansard in its c. 1890 photograph (T-2933). The rear range is '2B' (rear_wings).

construction.note: The 1911 sheet colours the building pink, its brick; the register reads the same ('Brick masonry').

principal_floor_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: a high stoop (T-1874's brief), the principal floor 1.8 m over grade on a stone foundation, higher than 1726's so the two fronts do not read as one; inside RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md's 1.2-2.0 m.

storey_heights_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: two tall brick storeys under the mansard, the principal storey the taller, inside the rules' ranges.

wall_thickness_front_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: a brick-and-a-half wall. The sheet prints '12' (inches) against each storey's wall, a 0.30 m brick wall; the K01 measure lays it at 0.33 with its pointing, as 1608's.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: as the front; the sheet's '12 12' is printed on the side walls.

service_wall_brick.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the K03 common brick panel 1608, 1616 and 1628 wear on every face; no picture of the house is known, so its brick's colour is the kit's.

basement_lights.note: RECONSTRUCTED: area lights in the stone foundation under the principal floor, the K06 area light without a well, as 1608's.

window_kit.note: RECONSTRUCTED: K06 two-over-two sash in recessed openings, the kit's ordinary period sash.

street_front_trim.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the recessed sash under flat stone lintels on both storeys (the brief's 'recessed sash under lintels'), a plainer head than 1726's hooded lintels, so the two fronts are distinct.

wall_head.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the K10 bracketed timber cornice under the mansard's curb, as the draft's row had it ('a bracketed cornice').

roof_form.note: The dashed line the 1911 sheet draws inside the front block, with its diagonals into the corners, is the plan of a mansard's curb and hips, and the walls' '12 12' put the third storey in the roof (stories). The draft drew it flat for want of a reading.

roof_pitch_deg.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the mansard's upper deck, nearly flat, as 1637's.

eave_overhang_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the K05 eave over the bracketed cornice.

mansard.note: RECONSTRUCTED: a convex (bell-cast) K05 mansard in slate, 2.8 m of lower face for the roof storey the sheet's '3B' counts, with a gabled dormer over each of the front's two window columns; 1637's dormers. The sheet gives the curb's plan (about 1 m inside the walls) and nothing of its section.

entrance_bay.note: The sheet's front: a one-storey brick vestibule at the south front corner ('1'), the open stoop beside it, and the entrance at the front's south end; the draft rules' row said south.

front_bays.note: Two columns along the front, south to north: the entrance and the windows over it at 1.6 m, and the frame bay's centre at 5.15 m (the sheet's bay at v 4.8-7.5 in the lot frame). The north 1.4 m is the corner pier against the lot line.

side_bays.note: RECONSTRUCTED: one window a storey in the south wall's run behind the projection (u 33.4-36.3); the projection carries the side's other lights. The north wall stands on the lot's north line and is blank, as K01 builds it.

north_bays.note: None: the north wall stands on the lot's north line (v 8.9 of 8.91), where the sheet draws no opening and no window could be had.

rear_bays.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the rear wall's windows over the two-storey rear range, in the mansard's rear face.

sash_by_storey.note: RECONSTRUCTED: tall sash to the tall storeys, the principal storey's the taller.

roof_covering.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the mansard's lower faces in Pennsylvania slate, its deck in painted standing-seam tin, copper flashings and roll, as 1637's.

chimneys.note: RECONSTRUCTED: two brick stacks on the north wall, the lot-line wall the flues of a narrow house rise in, through the mansard's cornice.

rainwater.note: RECONSTRUCTED: half-round copper gutters at the cornice, round downpipes to splash stones at the front's north corner, the south wall's rear corner and the rear.

entrance_kit.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the K07 panelled door at the head of a straight stoop, a high one (the principal floor at 1.8 m); the front wall stands 9.25 m from the walk (the lot's street line at u 55.15).

bays.note: Read off the 1911 sheet (s20fp-1730-b1), sizes in the lot frame. FRONT: a small canted bay coloured yellow, frame, on the front's north part (v 4.8-7.5, 0.85 m out), with no storey figure: built one storey, a frame bay window to the principal storey (as 1626's frame bay is two), its 1.5 m face holding one sash and its short cheeks blank; how its face and cheeks divide is RECONSTRUCTED. SOUTH: the front block stands 2.1 m further south from u 36.3 to the front (v 1.0 to -1.1); the sheet runs the mansard's dashed line into its middle (u 37.4-41.8) and prints '1' on its front end (u 41.8-45.9), so it is a two-storey projection under the roof with a one-storey brick vestibule at the front corner. K08 holds a projection to 1.2 m proud, so both are built 1.2 m out (0.9 m short), the projection 5.5 m long and the vestibule 3.8, stopped 0.3 m short of the front corner. Heights, windows and roofs RECONSTRUCTED.

rear_wings.note: The sheet's rear range, printed '2B' (the census row's 'rear 2B'): brick, the front block's full width (v 1.0-8.9) and 10.3 m deep (u 23.1-33.4), two storeys under a flat deck, its north wall on the lot line and blank; and the one-storey frame porch ('1', yellow) on its rear wall's north part (u 21.7-23.1, v 5.4-8.8), built closed in painted timber as 1613's is. Heights, deck and windows RECONSTRUCTED.

boundary.note: T-3205 (the owner, 2026-10-27: walks, gates and boundaries to the pictures). The only picture of 1730 in its own time, the May 1874 Land Owner vignette of A. A. Dewey's house (Prairie library a16-cgy-landowner-1874-1730-dewey, read from the image store's copy; not yet a source record here), draws a close-boarded fence along the whole street line, about as high as the basement, and no gate in it: K11's board fence 1.5 m just inside the street line (the 1904 parcel's, data/street_grid/1904.json prairie_1730), as 1616's front is built from the same issue's plate of 1620. The entrance gate on the walk, standing open, and the side gate across 1.6 m of the south yard's mouth at the lot line are the kit's; the vignette shows neither. RECONSTRUCTED: the fence kept from 1874 to 1904, its height and both gates (liberty L-k14-walks-1700-block-3205).

yard.note: T-3205 (the owner, 2026-10-27: walks, gates and boundaries to the pictures). The walk in flags from the stoop's foot through the entrance gate to the public walk; the cinder service walk from the side gate back along the south lot line, the gate's width. RECONSTRUCTED: the walk's flags, their width and wear, the lawn and its bare strip are the K14 kit's (data/components/prairie_1904/k14_condition.json) aged from the phase's own year, as the kit's rule is; liberty L-k14-walks-1700-block-3205.

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3B brick dwelling (D), the main block outlined by a dashed line; small frame porch on the south'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1840 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 20.
what_it_supplies: The Illinois Central / Michigan Central right-of-way and, from the 16th Street row south about 60 m, the water's edge beside it, as of 1911
Footprints, lot lines, street widths (66 ft; 16th Street 50 ft), addresses, material by colour and story counts for Indiana Av. to the tracks, 16th to 18th Street, as of 1911
Its own printed Scale of Feet, which the georeference uses as its scale
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: T-2934 (piece 2 of T-1874) refines the district draft (T-2334) in place under the same id: the house is rebuilt from the K01 frontage assembly and its kits — K03 brick on all four walls, K06 sash, K07 door and stoop, K08 bays and projections, K10 bracketed cornice, a K05 mansard with dormers — instead of the draft builder. What is read: the 1911 Sanborn sheet 20 (the front block '3B' with '12 12' walls and a mansard's plan drawn dashed inside them, the rear range '2B', brick, 'D', the bays, the vestibule and the porch drawn on the plan) through the T-1840 census, which rules it present in 1904. No photograph, plate or description of 1730 is known, so every elevation is the kits' (liberty L-k01-1726-1730-map-led-2934); a later reading that finds one replaces the kit's choices here.
